pairs.99 Days with NhiLe là một thử thách thể: 99 Days with NhiLe is a 99-day fitness challenge that invites Vietnamese people around the world to train together, improve their health and build healthy habits. It combines exercise with discipline: participants work out together at 4:45 am over Zoom, every day, for 99 days straight.
pairs.Thử thách này phù hợp cho mọi đối tượng,: The challenge suits everyone, from complete beginners to experienced athletes — anyone who wants better health and a healthy lifestyle. Focused on habit-building and perseverance, 99 Days with NhiLe creates an energising, inspiring training environment that helps participants build endurance and succeed in improving their overall fitness.

pairs.“99 Days with NhiLe” không chỉ là một th: "99 Days with NhiLe" is more than a fitness challenge — it is a journey of discipline and building a new way of living.
pairs.Mỗi sáng, bạn thức dậy lúc 4h45 AM, tham: Every morning you wake at 4:45 am and join the community workout on Zoom.
pairs.Mỗi ngày, bạn viết 3 điều biết ơn để nuô: Every day you write down 3 things you are grateful for, to nurture a positive mind.
pairs.Tâm trí sáng suốt, tinh thần lạc quan hơ: A clearer mind and a more optimistic spirit.
pairs.👉 Nói ngắn gọn: Đây là hành trình trở th: 👉 In short: this is the journey to a better version of yourself, one day at a time.
pairs.Đây còn là thử thách về kỷ luật cá nhân: It is also a personal-discipline challenge — where you learn to win over yourself every morning.
pairs.Thể dục chỉ là phương tiện. Mục tiêu thự: Exercise is only the vehicle. The real goal is building endurance and discipline.
pairs.Thỉnh thoảng chị NhiLe tham gia Zoom cùn: From time to time NhiLe joins the Zoom room after the workout ends.
pairs.Thời điểm cụ thể không cố định – như một: There is no fixed schedule — it is a surprise gift for those who always show up.
pairs.Bạn chỉ cần kiên trì và làm đúng quy địn: You only need to persevere and follow the rules every day.
pairs.Điều quan trọng không phải thể lực, mà l: What matters is not fitness but discipline — waking early, training and practising gratitude.
